quoted_clause: The break-even against a statically provisioned 21-host fleet ($420/hr) sits at 19 hosts
observed: The break-even calculation compares autoscaling cost (N×$20 + $40 fixed overhead) against static fleet cost (21×$20 = $420, no $40). The $40 is described as 'fixed overhead of ~$40/hr (infrastructure and staff)' which should apply to both fleets. If both incur $40, break-even is trivially at 21 hosts (N×20+40 = 21×20+40 → N=21). The stated break-even at 19 hosts only holds if the static fleet excludes the $40.
correction: Either (a) state explicitly that the $40 is autoscaling-specific overhead (scaling controller, scaling-decision monitoring) and not general infrastructure, or (b) apply the $40 to both fleets and recompute the break-even (which becomes trivially 21 hosts), or (c) reframe the comparison as autoscaling-with-overhead vs static-without-overhead and explain why the overhead differs.
acceptance_test: The break-even paragraph explicitly states which fleet(s) incur the $40 fixed overhead and the arithmetic is consistent with that statement.
verdict_evidence: ch20:76 costs autoscaling 21x$20+$40=$3.19/1K but static comparator '($420/hr)' = 21x$20, no $40.
fix_instruction: State the $40 is autoscaling-only control-plane overhead, or apply to both sides and restate break-even (21 hosts).

verdict_evidence: fig_ch20_capacity.py:58 legend 'analytical host capacity C_analytic = N x 17/8.6 (req/s)' on 'Fleet rate (req/s)' axis under title 'Fleet capacity vs host count'; quantity is fleet rate.
fix_instruction: Change the legend to 'analytical fleet capacity C_analytic = N x 17/8.6 (req/s)' and re-render fig-20-2001.

observed: The sentence is syntactically broken. The clause after the comma, “cost per request may decline,” is not grammatically connected to the preceding “where” clause, and the idea is repeated awkwardly.

page_hint: Ch 20 §3 "Autoscaling economics"; dependent anchors in Ch 21 §3, Ch 22 §6, Ch 23 §3, Ch 25 §3 and §6
quoted_clause: at the 40-rps peak the autoscaled fleet runs 21 hosts at (21 × $20 + $40) ÷ 144,000 requests/hr ≈ **$3.19 per 1K requests** ... The break-even against a statically provisioned 21-host fleet ($420/hr) sits at 19 hosts
observed: The chapter's own governing sizing is 23 hosts (case-(ii) prefill screen with the rho = 0.95 derate), but the entire economics block — cost per 1K requests at peak, cost per 1K at average, the ~28% average-cost decline, and the static-fleet break-even — is computed on 21 hosts, the case-(i) KV screen that the chapter explicitly says is not the fleet size. The same 21-host figure is then carried into other chapters as the canonical fleet size and into the canonical cost rows.
correction: Either (a) recompute the economics on the governing 23-host fleet and propagate 23 (and 34 under the full policy) to Ch 21 §3, Ch 22 §6, Ch 23 §3, Ch 25 §3 and Ch 25 §6, or (b) state explicitly in the economics block that the figures are computed on the 21-host KV-screen headline as a lower bound and that the governing 23-host fleet raises peak cost per 1K to ~$3.47 and moves the static break-even to ~41.5 rps. Whichever is chosen, add a one-line note in Ch 21 §3 and Ch 22 §6 that the $/1K rows inherit the host-count basis.
acceptance_test: Every host count used to derive a cost figure in Ch 20, 21, 22, 23 and 25 is either the governing screen or is explicitly labelled as a lower bound; the peak cost per 1K in Ch 20 §3 equals (governing hosts × $20 + $40) / 144,000.
verdict_evidence: Ch20:76 computes (21x$20+$40)/144,000 = $3.19 and 21-host break-even while :68/:164/:176 state 23 hosts governs; on 23: $3.47 (+9%), break-even 21 hosts/41.5 rps.
fix_instruction: Recompute section 3 economics on the governing 23-host fleet ($3.47/1K, break-even 41.5 rps) or label 21 as a lower bound; note the basis in Ch21/Ch22.

quoted_clause: The break-even against a statically provisioned 21-host fleet ($420/hr) sits at 19 hosts, i.e. sustained demand ≤ ~37.6 rps: above that, autoscaling costs more than the peak-sized fleet it replaces.
observed: The comparison is asymmetric: the autoscaled alternative is costed as (hosts x $20 + $40/hr) including the $40/hr fixed overhead, while the static alternative is costed as $420/hr with no overhead. The same infrastructure and staff overhead applies to a static fleet, so the static baseline is understated by $40/hr and the break-even is biased toward autoscaling.
correction: Apply the $40/hr overhead to both alternatives (or state explicitly that the static baseline excludes it and why), and recompute the break-even. If the overhead is genuinely avoided by a static fleet, say so and justify it.
acceptance_test: Both sides of the break-even comparison are costed on the same overhead basis, and the printed break-even demand can be reproduced from the printed inputs by a reader.
verdict_evidence: ch20:76 costs autoscaled fleet as N x$20+$40 but static baseline as $420/hr = 21x$20 no overhead; symmetric static 21 hosts = $460 -> N=21 -> 41.5 rps; 37.6 rps claim ~4 rps low.
fix_instruction: Cost both sides on one basis at ch20:76 (static 21 hosts = $460/hr -> break-even 21 hosts, 41.5 rps), or say why a static fleet avoids the $40/hr.

quoted_clause: | **Scheduling overhead** | Fraction of per-query time spent in dispatcher, not compute | < 5% of the 2 s turn budget (= 100 ms) |
observed: The metric's denominator (per-query time, i.e. the ~8.6 s service time) and the target's denominator (the 2 s TTFT turn budget) are different quantities. 5% of per-query time is ~430 ms, not 100 ms. As written, the row is internally inconsistent and cannot be measured as defined.
correction: Redefine the row as "Scheduler-added latency as a fraction of the TTFT budget" with target "< 5% of the 2 s turn budget (= 100 ms)", or keep the per-query-time definition and change the target to "< 5% of the 8.6 s service time (= 430 ms)" — but the latter contradicts the §3 absolute target, so the first is preferable.
acceptance_test: Every row of Table 20-1 has a definition and a target expressed over the same denominator, and the scheduling-overhead row agrees with the §3 paragraph.
verdict_evidence: ch20:93 defines metric as 'fraction of per-query time' (~8.6 s -> 430 ms) but targets '<5% of the 2 s turn budget (= 100 ms)'; :73 prose uses 2 s-TTFT denominator.
fix_instruction: Redefine the row as scheduler-added latency over the 2 s TTFT budget with target '<5% (= 100 ms)', matching ch20:73.

page_hint: Ch 20 §3, "Fleet aggregate throughput (illustrative form)", second bullet
quoted_clause: **Token-throughput screen → 11 hosts (non-binding).** The token-throughput ceiling gives ⌈40 / 3.684⌉ = 11 hosts, which stays non-binding here.
observed: One subsection earlier the chapter states that this exact division is invalid: "what makes the division wrong here is what its numerator mixes and its answer assumes, not its units" — the 35,000 tokens/s numerator is a phase-mixed prefill+decode total with no cost/phase-equivalence model. The chapter then performs the division and reports the result as a named screen, without repeating the caveat at the point of use.

verdict_evidence: ch20:35/:40 states 35,000/9,500 'not achievable here' and numerator phase-mixed; :60 runs ceil(40/3.684)=11 names it a screen, caveat unrepeated; absent from section 8 screen table.
fix_instruction: At ch20:60 relabel it as a non-binding artifact of a phase-mixed rate, not a valid screen without a phase-equivalence model, or delete the bullet.

page_hint: Ch 20 §3, "Simultaneous feasibility check (prefill + decode coexistence)" and "Fleet aggregate throughput"
quoted_clause: The ~93% leaves very little headroom before decode coexistence, interference, and the actual achieved MFU. ... with the standalone ρ = 0.95 derate applied to the prefill screen exactly as the policy arithmetic applies it, case (ii) rises to ⌈21.81 / 0.95⌉ = **23 hosts** — the largest requirement before the full policy
observed: The chapter never states the prefill utilization implied by its own governing sizing, and it treats the decode-coexistence headroom inconsistently. The feasibility check says there is essentially no headroom for decode coexistence at the KV-bound rate, yet the sizing applies only a 5% rho derate and calls 23 hosts governing. The reader is never told that the governing fleet is prefill-saturated.
correction: Add the implied prefill utilization to the screen table (per-host rate, prefill tokens/s, % of the case-(ii) ceiling) and state the consequence explicitly: the governing case-(ii) sizing is prefill-saturated, so decode coexistence requires either more hosts, a lower planning MFU, or P/D disaggregation. State whether the rho = 0.95 derate is intended to represent decode-coexistence headroom; if it is, say so and stop treating the 93% figure as evidence of no headroom.
acceptance_test: A reader can state, from Ch 20 alone, the prefill utilization at the governing host count and what that implies for decode coexistence on the same host.
verdict_evidence: Verified: 40/23=1.739 rps x9,200 = 16.0K tok/s = 94.8% of 16,870 case-(ii) ceiling; 22 hosts -> 99.2%; ch20:46 gives 93%/109% only at 2.0 rps stress screen; utilisation at governing 23 hosts never stated.
fix_instruction: Add per-host rate, prefill tok/s and % of the case-(ii) ceiling to ch20:58-68, and say the 23-host sizing is ~95% prefill-saturated.
